Monte Carlo as the Expected Derivative

Source: R/expect_method.R
expect_mc.Rd

Selects Monte Carlo as the method that obtains an expected derivative. The function draws nsim observations from the distribution at each parameter configuration, with distrib_rng(), and averages over them the quantity that identity names: $$\widehat{\mathbb{E}}[\partial^k \ell] = \frac{1}{n_{sim}} \sum_{m=1}^{n_{sim}} \partial^k \ell(y_m;\theta)$$ for identity = "hessian", the observed derivative of the requested order, and the same average of \(-\sum_{\pi} \prod_{B \in \pi} \ell_B(y_m;\theta)\) for identity = "score", the Bartlett partition identity (see expect_integrate() and expected_derivative_methods). Both estimate the same quantity as expect_integrate() with the same identity. The error decreases as \(1/\sqrt{n_{sim}}\), and the result is reproducible only if the seed is fixed. The cost is that of distrib_rng() times nsim, per distinct parameter configuration. The choice is adequate where quadrature performs poorly, as with heavy tails or an awkward support.

For a family with a non-smooth parameter (see param_smoothness()) the average of the observed second derivative omits the point mass at the kink, so that identity = "hessian" at order 2 signals an error that names identity = "score".

Usage

expect_mc(nsim = 10000, identity = c("hessian", "score"))

Arguments

nsim

The number of draws per parameter configuration, a single positive finite number. The default is 10000. A vector, a missing or non-finite value, or a number below 1 signals an error.

identity

One of "hessian" (the default) and "score". See the description and expected_derivative_methods.

Value

An S7 object of class ExpectMC, which inherits from ExpectMethod, with the properties nsim and identity.

See also

expect_opg() and expect_integrate() for the other methods; expected_derivative_methods for the comparison; distrib_deriv3(), distrib_deriv4(), distrib_expected_hessian() and fisher_scoring() for the functions that take the object.

Examples

a <- expect_mc(nsim = 2000)
a
#> Expectation by Monte Carlo (nsim = 2000)
expect_mc(nsim = 2000, identity = "score")
#> Expectation by Monte Carlo (nsim = 2000, identity = score)

# A sample is drawn at every call, so the seed fixes the result.
d <- gaussian1_distrib()
th <- list(mu = 0, sigma = 2)
set.seed(1)
distrib_deriv3(d, 0, th, expected = TRUE, method = a)$mu_mu_sigma
#> [1] 0.25

# The step of Fisher scoring can use the same object.
fisher_scoring(method = expect_mc(nsim = 1000))
#> Fisher scoring
#>   expected information: by Monte Carlo (nsim = 1000)
